1.1 Thil Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institutjon on 24 September 1966, after the draft finalized by the Water Sectional CJommittee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 1.2 Ice iI manufactured in a number of food industries, in cold storage plantlud exclusively in Ice-making industry. Good quality ice should be clear, colourl., free from air bubbles, snowy butts and heavy cores, It Iboulcl Dot abatter when handled. On melting, it should give a water of potable quality in ita bacteriological, physical and chemical features. Heaee the quality of water used in ice making is of utmost public health importance. I., In preparing this standard, assistance has been obtained from the

following publications:
; United States of America. California State Water Pollution Control Board. Mckee and Wolf. Water quality criteria. Ed 2 ( Publi� cation No. 3A). 1963. Sacramento. Special Technical Publication 148-D. ~1959. Manual on industrial water. Ed 2. American Society for Testing and Materials,

USA. 1.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this ltandard is complied with) the final value, observed or calculated, expressirig the result of a tot or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2�1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value Ihould be the same as that of the specified value in tilis standard.

1.1 Thia .tandard prescribes the quality tolerances for water used in ice manufacture.
